paper_title: Plasma proteomics for biomarker discovery in childhood tuberculosis
prediction_task: Binary classification of Confirmed TB vs Unlikely TB (non-TB respiratory disease) in children using plasma proteomic signatures from DIA-PASEF mass spectrometry (untargeted proteomics, case-control design, cross-sectional)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Every candidate model from the all-combinations search was evaluated on the 25% test set, effectively turning the test set into a second training step and inflating performance via multiple testing.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Conceded the caveat; added limitations-section statement that biosignatures were evaluated on a test set (not fully independent hold-out) and performance should be read as exploratory rather than confirmatory.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: LASSO cross-validation type, hyperparameters, and software details not specified; combinatorial 'linear' models were actually logistic regression, and scikit-learn call / CV scheme for feature selection unreported.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added 'Computational packages utilized' section, clarified LogisticRegression(penalty='l2') with default scikit-learn 1.5.1, corrected 'linear'->'logistic', published code on GitHub.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Two different imputation strategies applied at 50% and 10% missingness thresholds without rationale, and per-marker missingness (up to >70% for IGLL5, IGLV3-9) not originally reported, risking spurious biomarker selection.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Provided mechanistic rationale for dual imputation (detection-limit vs absent); re-ran biosignature with 50% missingness cap pre-LASSO, dropped IGLs, new 5/6-protein signatures at AUC 0.87/0.88.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: No independent validation cohort; 25% held-out split presented as 'validation' serves only bioinformatic role; generalization across countries/age/HIV subgroups untested.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Acknowledged lack of independent cohort; noted planned prospective validation several years away; added it as a future-direction limitation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: No subgroup analyses by age <2, sex, HIV, nutritional status despite significant HIV/malnutrition imbalance between TB and Unlikely TB groups (potential confounding of proteomic signature).
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Ran chi-square tests — HIV (p=0.033) and malnutrition (p=0.012) significantly associated with TB; added Table 1 statistics and limitation text; declined subgroup model refits due to sample size.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Only logistic regression evaluated; tree-based and non-linear methods not reported; rationale for restricting to logistic was post-hoc and results of other methods (XGBoost, RF, SVM) were 'data not shown'.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Stated NaiveBayes, SVM, RF, AdaBoost, XGBoost and ensembling were evaluated internally with similar performance; logistic chosen for interpretability and stability on small feature subsets.
